extracted.intended_audience: State Exchange administrators; QHP issuers and compliance officers; accrediting entities; HHS program staff
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedures for HHS's State Exchange Improper Payment Measurement (SEIPM) program and related QHP issuer/provider-access requirements, including sampling, review, dispute resolution, corrective action, and provider/network/ECP access rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and records HHS will use for SEIPM review
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS will review information related to QHP enrollment and APTC eligibility and payment determinations, including evidence of required data verifications, electronic sources consulted, timing and results of verifications, documentary evidence submitted by QHP enrollees, timing of submissions and adjudication, good faith extensions, redetermination information (automatic annual redeterminations, timing and results of periodic examinations of data sources, policy or application changes), and any consumer-submitted documents used to establish new or continued eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists the categories of case-level documentation State Exchanges must provide to HHS to support SEIPM review; includes both electronic verification results and copies of documentary evidence; applies to eligibility and enrollment actions affecting APTC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size calculation (aggregate across State Exchanges)
rubrics_metrics.description: At the beginning of each SEIPM cycle, HHS will calculate a sample size in aggregate across all State Exchanges using statistical methodology to estimate an improper payment rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample size is computed to estimate improper payment rate; HHS establishes minimum and maximum sample sizes to ensure statistical validity and operational feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-specific sample size determination factors
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS will develop sample sizes specific to each State Exchange and may consider overall APTC expenditures for the State Exchange, state-level precision goals for the current SEIPM cycle, and the State Exchange's prior improper payment rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States' sample sizes can differ based on expenditures, precision objectives, and historical error rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size parameters (minimum and maximum bounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS will establish minimum and maximum sample sizes to ensure statistical validity while maintaining operational feasibility across State Exchanges of varying sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to avoid too-small samples that lack statistical power and too-large samples that are operationally burdensome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample selection procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Annually, HHS will select samples of tax households from the data provided by each State Exchange as described in §155.1615(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is performed on an annual basis from the universe data submitted by State Exchanges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampled records notification contents
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS will notify each State Exchange of specific records selected for review and include the total number of sampled tax households selected for the State Exchange, a unique identifier for each sampled tax household, and any specific instructions or requirements needed to facilitate HHS' review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification gives State Exchanges the identifiers and logistical instructions to support review; must be provided within a specified timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of sampled records notification (60-day rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS will provide the sampled records notification no later than 60 days after receipt of complete universe data from all State Exchanges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes a firm timeline for informing States which records are sampled; see extension provision for exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of sampling notification timeline (grounds and procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS may extend the 60-day timeline if technical issues, data quality issues requiring additional coordination, or other circumstances beyond HHS's control prevent completion within the standard timeframe. If extended, HHS will notify affected State Exchanges in writing, provide the reason, and confirm any impact on subsequent SEIPM timelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits flexibility for legitimate delays but requires written notice and explanation to States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic review process for sampled records
rubrics_metrics.description: For each sampled record, HHS will conduct a comprehensive review of all information provided by the State Exchange using standardized review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews follow standardized protocols to ensure consistency across sampled records and State Exchanges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sources for HHS review
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews will use tax household information provided under §155.1615(b)(3), supplemented by relevant consumer-submitted documents gathered by the State Exchange as part of enrollment and eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS may rely on both State-submitted administrative data and documentary evidence submitted by consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error identification categories (APTC-related errors)
rubrics_metrics.description: The review will identify whether the State Exchange made errors resulting in improper payments related to: (i) enrolling or re-enrolling a consumer into a QHP for which APTC was paid; (ii) consumer eligibility for APTC being paid on the consumer's behalf; (iii) calculating the APTC amount that was paid on the consumer's behalf; and (iv) taking required actions upon changes to a consumer's status affecting APTC eligibility or payment amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly enumerates error types that constitute improper payments for APTC purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review standards and criteria (borrowing from subparts D and E)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS will apply consistent review standards based on the APTC-related determination requirements established in subparts D and E of this part, and other applicable provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews are grounded in the substantive eligibility/determination rules elsewhere in the regulations to ensure legal consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error evaluation: calculation of correct APTC
rubrics_metrics.description: For each error identified, HHS will calculate the correct APTC amount based on section 36B of the Internal Revenue Code and applicable implementing regulations, determine an improper payment amount, and document it within a Sampled Unit Assessment Package provided to the State Exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires use of tax-code-based calculations and documented case-level assessment packages shared with States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extrapolation methodology for estimating total improper payments
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS will extrapolate identified improper payments from the sample to estimate the total improper payment amount for the State Exchange's entire universe of APTC payments using statistically valid methodologies that comply with OMB guidance on improper payment estimation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimates must follow OMB improper payment guidance and appropriate statistical extrapolation techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual reporting of improper payment estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS will report annually in the Agency Financial Report the estimated aggregate improper payment rate for Federal and State Exchanges combined and the estimated aggregate improper payment rate for State Exchanges; HHS will also provide each State Exchange a report documenting the State-specific improper payment rate and error analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public reporting and State-specific reporting are required at least annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference Resolution process (State request timeline and scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: A State Exchange may submit a written Difference Resolution request within 30 days after issuance of the Sampled Unit Assessment Package to dispute HHS' error and improper payment findings; HHS will engage collaboratively, re-evaluate disputed findings using the same protocol, and prepare a Difference Resolution Decision communicated within 90 days of receiving the request, including analysis and rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Difference Resolution is an internal collaborative dispute mechanism with specified timelines (30-day filing, 90-day decision) and reuse of original review protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative appeal process (timing and limitations)
rubrics_metrics.description: To dispute a Difference Resolution Decision, a State Exchange may file a written administrative appeal within 15 business days after issuance of the Difference Resolution Decision; the State may not submit new evidence (but may provide additional context for previously submitted evidence). HHS will assign reviewers not involved in the original review, conduct an independent review using the administrative record, and issue an appeal decision within 90 days based on a preponderance of the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals are time-limited, evidence is generally limited to the record, reviewers are independent of the original review, and the standard of decision is preponderance of evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference Resolution and administrative appeal submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests must be filed in a form and manner specified by HHS and must contain a clear statement of the specific finding(s) being challenged, all factual and legal bases for the request, and evidence directly related to the findings (including clarifying data interpretation or legal citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies required content for submissions so HHS can process disputes; failure to provide required elements may affect consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of adjustments and amended reporting after successful disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: If Difference Resolution or appeals are resolved in favor of the State Exchange during the current SEIPM cycle, HHS will adjust affected improper payment rate calculations for the cycle and reflect updated aggregate rates in current-cycle reporting; if resolved after completion of the cycle, HHS may publish amended aggregate improper payment rates and notify affected State Exchanges if material changes occur, or decline to amend if changes are not material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes how winning disputes affect current and past reported estimates and when HHS will publish amended reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good cause exception for timeline extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: For good cause, HHS may extend timelines for accepting Difference Resolution or administrative appeals or for issuing decisions; HHS's failure to timely issue a decision does not indicate acceptance of the State's position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides limited flexibility for timing while clarifying that delays don't automatically favor the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective Action Plan (CAP) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS may require a State Exchange to develop and submit a proposed CAP to correct errors resulting in improper payments; the CAP must address errors included in the State Exchange improper payment report and be developed in accordance with HHS requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CAPs are mandatory when HHS requires them and must be tailored to the State-specific errors identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: CAP development: error analysis and root cause identification
rubrics_metrics.description: In developing a proposed CAP, the State Exchange must conduct an error analysis reviewing causes, characteristics, and frequency of errors; determine causes of the errors in the improper payment rate and identify root causes of resulting improper payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires analytical review of error patterns to inform corrective measures; if appeals are pending, HHS may provide a revised CAP timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: CAP required contents for each identified error
rubrics_metrics.description: For each identified error, the proposed CAP must include the specific corrective action, status of the corrective action, scheduled or actual implementation date, key personnel responsible, and a plan for monitoring the effectiveness of the corrective action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CAPs must include measurable milestones, accountability mechanisms, monitoring and validation, documentation of implemented actions, and regular status updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: CAP implementation and evaluation schedule and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: A State Exchange must develop an implementation schedule, implement the CAP according to that schedule, regularly evaluate effectiveness in reducing/eliminating error causes, and provide updates on CAP progress at least annually or in a manner and frequency specified by HHS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes ongoing evaluation and periodic reporting on CAP progress; HHS may require more frequent updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failures in the CAP process and HHS actions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a State Exchange does not submit a required CAP, submits an incomplete CAP not addressing required parts, fails to follow the implementation schedule, or submits an unacceptable CAP after technical assistance, HHS may take actions consistent with §155.1650 (remedial and escalation measures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncompliance with CAP obligations can trigger remedial measures including enhanced oversight and potential escalation.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEIPM preparation phase for new State Exchanges
rubrics_metrics.description: Any State Exchange in its first year must participate in a 1-year SEIPM preparation phase prior to participating in SEIPM in the subsequent year; to satisfy requirements, a State Exchange must complete information submissions using most current Plan Year data for a sample not to exceed 10 unique tax households addressing HHS-specified scenarios, undergo review procedures per §155.1625(a) and (b), and participate in HHS technical assistance (training, system readiness, data validation, process improvement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New Exchanges receive a testing/preparation cycle with limited sample size and technical assistance to ensure readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimization of duplicate audit requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS will minimize duplicate requirements between the annual independent external programmatic audit (§155.1200(c) and (d)) and SEIPM so that completing SEIPM may satisfy certain audit review requirements, particularly review of compliance with subparts D and E, as identified in HHS sub-regulatory guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intends to reduce redundant state burden by allowing SEIPM results to substitute for parts of other required audits as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of improper payments when State fails to provide adequate documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: For improper payment measurement purposes, HHS will classify APTC payments as improper when a State Exchange fails to provide adequate documentation demonstrating payments were made in accordance with applicable Federal requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Places evidentiary burden on State Exchanges to document compliance; absence of documentation may be treated as an improper payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of substantial noncompliance (criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS will determine that a State Exchange has failed to substantially comply if the State Exchange: (1) fails to submit required data/documentation within Annual Program Schedule timelines; (2) submits incomplete, inaccurate, or improperly formatted data that reasonably prevents effective review; (3) fails to implement the CAP process as set out; or (4) demonstrates a pattern of more than five instances during a SEIPM cycle of non-response within 30 calendar days to HHS requests for clarification or additional information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates specific acts/omissions that constitute substantial noncompliance and may trigger notices/remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to cure noncompliance (30-day minimum)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before implementing remedial measures for noncompliance, HHS will provide written notice specifying nature of noncompliance and potential consequences and allow a reasonable opportunity, not less than 30 days, to cure or demonstrate compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due-process step before enforcement actions; minimum cure period is 30 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial measures HHS may implement for noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If a State Exchange fails to substantially comply and such failures undermine HHS administration of improper payment measurement activities, HHS may implement enhanced monitoring and reporting, mandatory implementation of specific operational procedures or controls, and on-site visits to assess operations and data systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a menu of escalatory compliance activities HHS may deploy before more severe sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Escalation procedures including revocation of authority
rubrics_metrics.description: If a State Exchange continues to fail to comply after initial remedial measures, HHS may initiate proceedings to revoke the State Exchange's authority to operate in accordance with applicable law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revocation is the ultimate escalation for persistent noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index rate considerations for single risk pool (plan-level factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Index rate may account for the plan's provider network, delivery system characteristics, utilization management practices, and for catastrophic plans with multi-year terms, the length of the entire term to account for benefit characteristics (deductible, maximum out-of-pocket structure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When setting index rates, issuers/analysts must consider network/delivery/utilization and term length for multi-year catastrophic plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential health benefits (EHB) exclusions (timing for specified items)
rubrics_metrics.description: For plan years beginning before January 1, 2026, issuers may not include routine non-pediatric dental services, routine non-pediatric eye exam services, long-term/custodial nursing home care benefits, or non-medically necessary orthodontia as EHB. For plan years in 2026, and for plan years on/after Jan 1, 2027, the rule also bars specified sex-trait modification procedures as EHB (definition at §156.400).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies categories that may not be included as EHB, with phased effective dates adding specified sex-trait modification procedures by 2026/2027.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-sharing limits and special rule for multi-year catastrophic plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as permitted in §156.136, cost sharing may not exceed statutory maxima for plan years after 2014; for catastrophic plans with consecutive multi-year terms, the annual limitation on cost sharing for the initial plan year may apply annually or be averaged over the life of the contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides flexibility on how annual limits apply for multi-year catastrophic contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expanded cost-sharing parameters for bronze plans (§156.136)
rubrics_metrics.description: For plan years beginning on/after Jan 1, 2027, an issuer offering a bronze plan that complies with §156.130 and §156.140 may also offer within the same service area bronze plans that exceed the maximum annual limitation on cost sharing in increments of $50 to achieve an AV within the standard bronze de minimis variation, calculated per §156.135.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits incremental higher cost-sharing bronze variants to achieve actuarial value targets within de minimis ranges, subject to conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enrollment rules for catastrophic plans (benefit and term limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Catastrophic plans must meet applicable individual market requirements and for plan years beginning before Jan 1, 2027, provide EHB only after the annual limitation on cost sharing is reached; for plan years beginning on/after Jan 1, 2027, the threshold is 130% of the annual limitation on cost sharing rounded down to the next $50 multiple. Catastrophic plans may have plan terms of 1 year or multiple consecutive years not to exceed 10 years, and multi-year plans of at least 2 years may utilize value-based insurance designs to provide preventive service benefits before the enrollee satisfies the deductible or annual limitation on cost sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines allowable plan-term structures, pre-deductible preventive benefit flexibility for multi-year catastrophic plans, and modified cost-sharing thresholds for 2027+.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider access standards for network plans (§156.230)
rubrics_metrics.description: A QHP using a provider network must ensure its in-network providers, available to all enrollees, meet provider access standards, including meeting adequacy metrics; issuers in Federally-facilitated Exchanges in States without an Effective Provider Access Review Program must comply with specified requirements and provide justifications if network adequacy standards are not met. CMS may grant exceptions when making a plan available is in the interests of qualified individuals. A limited exception applies to stand-alone dental plans in areas 'prohibitively difficult' as attested by State departments of insurance for CEAC counties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires demonstration of network adequacy, justification and remediation plans if standards not met, and limited exceptions for stand-alone dental plans in extreme-access areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification requirement when network adequacy unmet
rubrics_metrics.description: If a QHP applying for certification in a Federally-facilitated Exchange does not satisfy network adequacy standards, the issuer must include in its application a justification describing how the network provides adequate service and how it will be strengthened to comply prior to the plan year, and provide information as requested by the FFE to support this justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires concrete remedial commitments and supporting information when an issuer falls short of network standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential Community Provider (ECP) standards for network plans (§156.235)
rubrics_metrics.description: A QHP issuer with a provider network must ensure the network includes a sufficient number and geographic distribution of ECPs, where available, to ensure reasonable and timely access for low-income individuals or those in Health Professional Shortage Areas. A plan has sufficient ECPs if the network includes at least minimum percentages (specified by HHS) of available ECPs across categories and within certain categories; multiple providers at one location count as a single ECP; in tiered networks, providers must be contracted within the lowest-cost tier to count toward ECP standards; the plan must report status of contract offers to qualified ECPs in its application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets quantitative and counting rules for ECP inclusion, tiering implications, and application reporting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate ECP standard for issuers relying on employed/contracted medical groups
rubrics_metrics.description: A network plan that provides most services through physicians employed by the issuer or a single contracted medical group may comply with an alternate standard requiring a sufficient number and distribution of employed/contracted providers and hospital facilities to ensure access; the plan must demonstrate minimum percentages of providers located in HPSAs or high-poverty zip codes and that the integrated delivery system provides all categories of services or offers contracts to at least one ECP outside the system per category per county.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an alternate path for large integrated systems to meet ECP obligations, with specific geographic and service-category tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider access and ECP standards for non-network plans (§156.236)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-network plans must ensure access to a range of providers that accept the plan's benefit amount as payment in full, including ECPs and mental health/substance-use-disorder providers; simply providing a benefit amount without other contextual information does not constitute access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-network plans must demonstrate substantive access safeguards beyond nominal benefit levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information non-network plans must submit for QHP certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-network plans applying for QHP certification must submit: assessed percentage of providers in each service area that accept the plan's benefit amount as payment in full and ECP compliance at HHS-specified minimums; whether at least one ECP per eight ECP categories per county accepts payment in full; whether all available Indian health care providers accept payment in full; outreach strategies to providers; strategy for publicizing benefit amounts; methodology for determining benefit amounts; strategies for consumer information about balance billing and historical out-of-pocket data; availability of an exceptions process for enrollees who cannot find accepting providers; and customer service/online provider directory assistance strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nine explicit submission items that non-network plans must provide to demonstrate reasonable/timely access and transparency about payment and balance-billing risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accreditation requirement: provider access consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Provider access standards for accreditation used by recognized accrediting entities must at minimum be consistent with the general requirements for network plans (§156.230(a)(2) and (3)) and for non-network plans (§156.236(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accrediting entities must align their provider access standards to the regulatory network and non-network minimums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audits and compliance reviews of QHP issuers (§156.480)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS or its designee may audit or conduct compliance reviews of an issuer offering a QHP through an Exchange to assess compliance with requirements related to ADP, CSRs, and user fee programs; compliance reviews will follow standards set forth in §156.715.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuers are subject to federal audit/compliance review for administration of premium tax credits, cost-sharing reductions, and user fee programs, per §156.715 procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances requiring HHS enforcement and civil money penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: If HHS determines a State Exchange or State-based Exchange on the Federal platform is not enforcing or fails to substantially enforce requirements related to administration of APTC, CSRs, and user fee programs, HHS may enforce and may pursue civil money penalties as specified in §156.805 for noncompliance by QHP issuers participating in that Exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables HHS to step in and impose penalties when State enforcement is inadequate; cross-references to §156.805 for CMP procedures and factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of sanctions applicable to QHP issuer noncompliance (§156.800)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sanctions under subpart I are applicable for noncompliance with QHP issuer participation standards and other standards applicable to issuers offering QHPs in a Federally-facilitated Exchange; these sanctions may also apply to issuers in State Exchanges and State-based Exchanges on the Federal platform when HHS is responsible for enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines reach of sanction authority, including where HHS assumes enforcement responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors in determining amount of civil money penalties (§156.805(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining CMP amount, HHS will identify lawful purposes of the penalty and take into account relevant factors as appropriate to the circumstances of the case (factors are not fully enumerated in this chunk but referenced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMP calculation is fact-specific and considers statutory/legal purposes and contextual factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances requiring HHS enforcement in State Exchanges (§156.805(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS will enforce requirements applicable to issuers in State Exchanges or State-based Exchanges on the Federal platform if the State with enforcement authority notifies HHS it is not enforcing or if HHS determines the State is failing to substantially enforce using processes in 45 CFR 150.201 et seq.; HHS may impose CMPs on an issuer in such an Exchange in accordance with this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies triggers for HHS intervention in State-regulated Exchanges and the authority to impose penalties on issuers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decertification bases and process reference (§156.810 amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: §156.810 (Bases and process for decertification of a QHP offered by an issuer through a Federally-facilitated Exchange) is amended (paragraph content not fully shown in the chunk).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory amendment indicates modified/clarified decertification bases/process; users should consult the full amended §156.810 text for details.
